items.title: NEW — a const-eval END-OF-EVALUATION HOOK: a const-time function can SCHEDULE a callback to run once after every const evaluation of the build has finished (repeat scheduling of the same callback is idempotent — it runs once), so a module can accumulate into a global during evaluation and process + emit the result in one go at the end. The first consumer is styling (B308, RULED): `Style::rule` stops emitting at construction and appends to a registry; the scheduled finaliser drops what no applied class references and emits the stylesheet once — which dissolves the 'X is already emitted before Y is known' class instead of retracting it. Owner: 'a proper build step hook for styling would fix the issue for good'
items.discussion: the owner's ruling on style-conditions.md §10 (vi) (2026-09-13); B308 re-pointed here; A95's build takes it as its first brick (every later slice's emission is simpler once emission is late). The integrator had pushed back on a build hook before (Order 33, B308's retraction design) — withdrawn
items.body: **Mechanism.** A const-eval intrinsic `schedule_at_end(f: || void)` (name to settle): records `f` by identity in the evaluator's finaliser list (a set — a second request for the same function is a no-op), and after the LAST const evaluation of the build the evaluator runs the list in registration order, each once, in a const context (so `emit` and the globals are reachable). Questions the build answers: what 'the end' is under incremental/HMR rounds (per round: the round's finalisers run at its end; a module that did not re-evaluate does not re-schedule — its emitted asset is retained by the round's artifact record, B276/M59's machinery); ordering between two modules' finalisers (registration order; document it); a finaliser that panics (the build fails naming the finaliser's function). **Styling on it.** `Style::rule` → `registry.push(rule)`; `class_list`/application marks a class LIVE; the finaliser emits the rules of live classes in the band order and drops the rest — B308's dead sets vanish without retraction, and A95's canonicaliser runs over complete sets. Pins: idempotent scheduling (three requests, one run), run-once-at-end (a finaliser sees every rule pushed after its scheduling), the HMR round (a re-evaluated module re-emits, an untouched one is retained), the panic; styling: B308's nested exhibit emits exactly the applied rules (the `hmr_css_matrix`/`ssr_differential` gates hold), the compact-styling numbers (css-block §15.3) re-measured.
